issue_context.title: Draco decoding errors result in uncaught promise rejections.
comments:
Thanks for the report!

I agree we should try to get GLTFLoader to not call the older `decodeDracoFile` method. Using `decodeGeometry` looks like a good choice, although I'm not sure we want to expose the details of the `taskConfig` object, maybe the method signature should change to hide that.

Aside — the error sounds like your Draco-compressed data contains points and not just triangles, which wouldn't ordinarily be valid in the glTF Draco extension... is that something you're aware of?

OK, that makes sense. I could do that. Something similar to `decodeDracoFile`? I'm not sure of the protocol for breaking changes - is that a concern?

Thanks for the note. I'm making these models elsewhere programatically, so I'm pretty sure they don't actually contain points. Might chopping off an arbitrary number of characters at the end of the data url cause such a misread? I did get a variety of other errors trying to create a smaller failing demo string.

It'd be OK to keep `decodeDracoFile` around in its current form for now, and just have GLTFLoader use a different method. So no breaking change until we eventually decide to remove the deprecated method. 👍

> Might chopping off an arbitrary number of characters at the end of the data url cause such a misread?

Ah, it might. I'm not sure how the internals of the Draco decoder works but it sounds plausible.

@donmccurdy Sorry for the delay, but I'm hoping to get back to this and resolve it. I'm uncertain how to follow your comment though:

> Using `decodeGeometry` looks like a good choice, although I'm not sure we want to expose the details of the `taskConfig` object, maybe the method signature should change to hide that.

(methods in question: https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/dev/examples/jsm/loaders/DRACOLoader.js#L91-L203)

My best guess is this, but maybe I'm missing something:

1. Creating a third method (`decodeDracoGeometry`?) with the preferred signature: `decodeDracoGeometry( buffer, attributeIDs, attributeTypes, useUniqueIds )`.
2. Move the contents of `decodeGeometry` into the new method.
3. Make `decodeGeometry` call the new method, as `decodeDracoFile` does now.

Thanks!

I think we may need to overhaul DRACOLoader a bit anyway (see https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/issues/22445 ...) and have it use the new WorkerPool utility. Probably better to resolve this all at the same time, I'll self-assign it in that case.

I've run into a similar unhandled promise rejection error with DRACO decoding in some environments where there isn't enough memory for the wasm decoder to run properly. I get an unhandled promise rejection with `memory access out of bounds`. I can setup an example that illustrates the problem if needed but it's similar to what's described in the issue. 

It would be great if I could handle the error properly and fallback to something else. Is there an update on this issue?
I've unassigned myself here, as I haven't found time to work on DRACOLoader. I think PRs fixing the issue would be welcome.

review_comments: nit: I think the catch-and-then-throw block is not really doing anything, won't we have the same behavior with or without it? If there's a special purpose for this we may need to call it out in a comment.

Good point. Yes, I think the relevant addition is the new `catch()` when calling `decodeGeometry()`. This block here seems indeed redundant.

@Benjythebee Can you confirm?

I apologize, I believe I did this for my own sanity while debugging this;
I can 100% send another PR to remove this portion of the code. Let me know!
https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/pull/27308 feel free to mark as PR and merge; Close if not good
